14/ Dated 11.08.2023  Heard the parties.

Ms. Sharda Kumari, learned Amicus Curiae appearing on behalf of the petitioner has drawn the attention of this Court towards Exhibit-A & Exhibit-B, by virtue of which, it transpires that the parties have resolved their matrimonial dispute.
It further transpires that both the parties are residing separately and the informant has received her dower.

Ms. Satya Satakshi, learned Amicus Curiae for the informant after going through the records has stated that the parties have settled their dispute, but she has stated that it was after the recording of evidence of the informant and her witnesses.

Petitioner Salim @ Salim Ansari has filed this application against the judgment dated 06.07.2011 passed by Sri Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, learned Sessions Judge, Giridih (as His Lordship was the then) in Cr. Appeal No.13/2010, whereby and wherein, learned Sessions Judge, Giridih dismissed the appeal of the petitioner by upholding the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 18.01.2010 passed by Sri Taufeeq Ahmed, learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st class, Giridih in connection with G.R. Case No.1233/2005, arising out of Gandey P.S. Case No. 50/2005, holding the petitioner guilty of offence under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and thereby, sentencing him to undergo R.I for two years along- with a fine of Rs.1,000/-.
In default of payment of fine, he was further directed to undergo imprisonment for three months.
The prosecution case was instituted on the basis of a complaint case filed by the informant Nuresha Bano, alleging therein that she was married to the petitioner on 17.03.1996.

sentences.text: To enforce the demand, she was tortured and ultimately she was driven away from matrimonial home on 14.07.2004.
The complaint petition was sent to Gandey Police Station for institution of the F.I.R under Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C.
In order to prove its case, the prosecution has adduced oral evidence.
The petitioner has adduced documentary evidence to show that the parties had settled their dispute.

On the basis of evidence of both oral and documentary available on record, both the learned Appellate Court and the learned Trial Court came to a concurrent finding regarding the guilt of the petitioner.
The informant Nuresha Khatoon, who has been examined as P.W.5, has stated that her marriage was solemnized with the petitioner eleven years ago.
She gave birth to two children.
She has stated that the accused persons were demanding Rs.25,000/- from her.
To enforce the demand, she was tortured and ultimately, she was driven away from matrimonial home.
In her cross-examination, she has stated that she cannot state the date, on which, the demand of Rs.25,000/- was made.
She has denied that she was been divorced on the intervention of local panchayat.
P.W.1 Md. Hadish is the father of the informant.
He has supported the fact that the marriage between the parties was solemnized in the year 1996 as per Muslim Rights and Customs.
He has further stated that after marriage, the petitioner started demanding Rs.25,000/- and to enforce the demand, she was tortured and ultimately, she was driven away from matrimonial home.

In his cross-examination, he has admitted that the parties have decided to separate, due to which,
the petitioner had divorced his daughter and Rs.30,000/- was to be paid as dower.
He has stated that dower should be given to his daughter.
Jalil Mian P.W.2, Md Gyasuddin P.W.3 and Abdul Qadir P.W.4 have stated that the petitioner was married to the informant.
Petitioner used to demand of Rs.25,000/-.
All these witnesses appear to be the hearsay witnesses.

From perusal of the documentary evidence adduced by the petitioner, it appears that the issue between the petitioner and the informant was resolved and on the basis of the decision taken in the local Panchayat, the petitioner had divorced the informant.
It appears from perusal of the document, which is Exhibit-B that the informant has received Rs.30,000/- from the petitioner as dower on 24.12.2004.
From the aforesaid oral and documentary evidence, it is apparent that the informant has made a general, vague and omnibus allegations regarding the demand of dowry against the petitioner.
She has failed to state the date and time when the demand was made.
There is no specific averment regarding the torture meted out to her by the petitioner.

sentences.text: From perusal of the written compromise made between the parties, which is Exhibit-A, it appears that there was marital dispute between the parties and both the parties had decided to live separately, by the virtue of which, the petitioner had divorced the informant.
It also appears that dower has also been paid.

Considering the aforesaid facts, I am of the opinion that the prosecution has not been able to prove its case against the petitioner for committing offence under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code beyond all reasonable doubts.
Accordingly, this revision application is allowed.
Pending I.A., if any, also stands disposed of.

Before parting, I will like to record my appreciation for Ms. Sharda Kumari and Ms. Satya Satakshi,
both the Amici Curie, who have very ably assisted this Court.

The Member Secretary, JHALSA is directed to pay Rs.5,000/- each to Ms. Sharda Kumari and Ms. Satya Satakshi, learned Amici Curie,
who have rendered their services in this case.
BS/ (Ambuj Nath, J.)
